answer: Each established key gets one invite token at open. A first submit is dropped unless it burns a token from an unrelated established key. Tokens expire at close and cannot be split, lent, or saved. The protocol publishes remaining R and burn P = U * I0 / R, U this epoch's per-head payout and I0 issued at open. The first head pays near U; the tenth pays more because nine tokens are already gone. Fresh keys receive none and cannot reset R. The burn sits in a kernel of leftover payout, the spent token is the only valid anchor, and a plume of aliases prints none.
